title: Viscoelastic sphere breathing resonances: radial drive vs the spherical Bessel solution (frequency response, analytic)
description:
A free viscoelastic sphere (radius a = 10 mm, rho 1100 kg/m^3; relaxed shear modulus G0 = 1 MPa, bulk modulus K0 = 3 MPa, mechanical_loss_factor eta = 0.05 on both, one shear Prony branch G1 = 1 MPa, tau1 = 60 us) driven by a harmonic radial body force f = f0 r_vec / a (f0 = 1e5 N/m^3 at the surface; the shape of self-gravity), axisymmetric (r, z) with the centre on the axis at z_c = 1.2 a in a 1.2 a x 2.4 a window of void (no material outside: the surface is free, nothing truncated). solid_mechanics on quadratic triangles (h = a/16 inside the sphere), displacement formulation, no support: a free body is regular at f > 0; the drive has no net axial force, so the rigid axial motion stays ~1e-6 of the peak (u_y of the equator probes) and the probes read u_r = u_x on the equator z = z_c, which an axial translation leaves untouched. frequency_response from 1.5 to 8 kHz in 100 Hz steps across the first two breathing (l = 0) resonances.
Why a body force: a uniform surface pressure is the textbook drive, but solid_mechanics has no normal-pressure load on a curved boundary (boundary_load acts on outer faces in model axes, segment_load on line objects). The linear radial body force gives the same resonance denominator: u - c r below is exactly the response to a surface pressure P = 3 K* c.
Analytic (exp(+j omega t)): G*(w) = G0 (1 + j eta) + G1 j w tau1 / (1 + j w tau1), K* = K0 (1 + j eta), M* = K* + 4/3 G*, lam* = K* - 2/3 G*, k = w sqrt(rho / M*). u_r solves M* (u'' + 2 u' / r - 2 u / r^2) + rho w^2 u = -f0 r / a: u = c r + A j1(k r) with c = -f0 / (rho w^2 a) (the vector Laplacian annihilates c r; its stress is the uniform 3 K* c I), and the free surface sigma_rr = M* u' + 2 lam* u / r = 0 at r = a gives A = -3 K* c / D, D = M* k j1'(k a) + 2 lam* j1(k a) / a (spherical_jn(1, z, 1) = j1'). The resonances are the complex roots of D(w) = 0: with the relaxed real moduli (eta = 0, branch frozen out) k a = 2.7812 and 6.1300 (2778 and 6123 Hz); with the branch and eta (Newton on D in float64) f = 2842.687 + 115.691j Hz (Q = Re f / (2 Im f) = 12.286) and 6831.081 + 398.175j Hz (Q 8.58): the branch stiffens G' (the shift up) and its loss G1 w tau1 / (1 + (w tau1)^2) dominates eta (the width). Hoop stress sigma_phiphi = lam* u' + 2 (lam* + G*) u / r (stress_zz; at the equator equal to sigma_thetatheta = stress_yy). The closed form was checked apart from the FEM: the ODE residual by finite differences (2e-8 of f0), sigma_rr(a) = 0 (7e-10), and the static limit u(a) = -f0 a^2 / (10 M) + f0 a^2 (3 M + 2 lam) / (30 K M) approached as (f / f_1)^2.
Curves & tables tab: probe_surface (r = a) and probe_mid (r = a/2) u_x_re / u_x_im versus frequency over their analytic curves (u_x_abs / _phase show the peak and the phase turn). Derived values tab: u_surface_peak and u_surface_peak2 = |u_r(a)| at the samples nearest the two peaks (2.8 and 7.0 kHz; the second is 40x lower and barely weighs in the curve errors); f_breathing_1 / q_breathing_1 = pole_fit of the surface response over 2 - 3.8 kHz against the first complex root (the one-pole + linear-background model is itself biased by 1.9e-5 / 2.0e-5: the same fit of the exact samples gives the same numbers; the broad second root is not graded: there that fit is off by 2 % in f and 17 % in Q even on exact samples); hoop_mid_8kHz = stress_zz at r = a/2 of the last frequency (the live field). Field tab: u_x and stress_zz of 8 kHz.
Expected agreement: the body force is one value per element (its centroid), which limits the convergence to O(h^2) (P2 alone would be faster). Mesh study h = a/8, a/16, a/32 (curve error = max |FEM - analytic| / ptp): Re curves 8.6e-4, 1.8e-4, 4.5e-5; Im curves 1.4e-3, 3.2e-4, 8.0e-5; u_surface_peak 1.5e-3, 3.2e-4, 8.1e-5; u_surface_peak2 3.6e-3, 8.9e-4, 1.9e-4; hoop_mid_8kHz 1.1e-2, 3.0e-3, 5.9e-4; the pole fit 1.9e-5 / 2.0e-5 at every h (its own bias). Tolerances (h = a/16): curves 1e-3, u_surface_peak 1e-3, u_surface_peak2 3e-3, f / q 1e-4, hoop 1e-2. The mixed formulation (P2 / P1, finite K*) gives the same displacements (to 5e-6 of the peak; hoop 4.7e-3: the stress takes the P1 pressure) at 1.7x the time.

parameters.name: eta_s
parameters.description: mechanical loss factor (on G0 and K0)

parameters.name: tau_1
parameters.description: shear Prony branch relaxation time [s] (w tau = 1 at 2.65 kHz)

parameters.name: f0
parameters.description: radial body force amplitude at r = a [N/m^3] (f = f0 r_vec / a)

parameters.name: z_c
parameters.description: height of the sphere centre on the axis

parameters.name: f_pk
parameters.description: swept frequency nearest the first peak [Hz]

parameters.name: f_pk2
parameters.description: swept frequency nearest the second peak [Hz]

parameters.name: f_root1
parameters.description: Re of the first complex root of D [Hz] (Newton, float64)

parameters.name: Q_root1
parameters.description: Re f / (2 Im f) of the first root

derived_values.name: u_surface_peak
derived_values.reference: abs((-f0/(rho_s*(2*pi*f_pk)**2*a_s))*(a_s - 3*K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s)*spherical_jn(1, (2*pi*f_pk*sqrt(rho_s/(K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + 4*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)))*a_s)/((K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + 4*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)*(2*pi*f_pk*sqrt(rho_s/(K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + 4*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)))*spherical_jn(1, (2*pi*f_pk*sqrt(rho_s/(K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + 4*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)))*a_s, 1) + 2*(K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) - 2*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)*spherical_jn(1, (2*pi*f_pk*sqrt(rho_s/(K0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + 4*(G0*(1 + 1j*eta_s) + G1*2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1/(1 + 2j*pi*f_pk*tau_1))/3)))*a_s)/a_s)))
